title: Dévissage des complexes ½ simpliciaux ∂ - parfaits et structures multiplicatives… (1975 ou 1976) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
The page is almost empty. The faint writing visible over most of it is show-through from the other side of the sheet, not text belonging to this page. The only text is two lines in blue ink at the top. A plausible reading is: "Il y a donc un complexe de De Rham–Sullivan si la car. [est] 0" ("so there is a De Rham–Sullivan complex if the characteristic is 0"). Above the line, "si la car." seems to be inserted in place of a crossed-out word beginning "co…"/"en…".

Context from the previous page: Grothendieck is building a 'De Rham complex ∂-p.' attached to semi-simplicial (cosimplicial) ∂-perfect objects. It is a bigraded algebra object, whose strict anticommutativity he cannot yet assert without a divided-power ('p.d.') structure. In fixed total degree it should give a Σ-regular (flasque-type) resolution of the constant object k_* = Ψ⁰_*, with top degree Ψⁿ_* = Λⁿ Ψ_*. He uses this to compare the multiplicative structure obtained by transport through R with that of the cochain complex C.

The note on this page draws the conclusion. In characteristic 0 the divided-power problem disappears, since x^n/n! makes sense. The construction then gives a genuine strictly commutative DGA model of cochains, i.e. Sullivan's polynomial de Rham forms A_PL. In positive characteristic one needs the divided-power version.

The next page starts an unrelated topic, 'catégories polynômiales'.
errors: No mathematical content to check. The claim that a commutative De Rham–Sullivan model exists in characteristic 0 is correct (Sullivan; Bousfield–Gugenheim). In characteristic p, strictly commutative cochain models cannot exist because of Steenrod operations, which is consistent with Grothendieck's restriction.

ideas.what: Existence of a De Rham–Sullivan (polynomial forms) complex as a commutative cochain model, conditional on characteristic 0, as the end point of his divided-power De Rham construction on semi-simplicial objects
ideas.modern_name: Sullivan's A_PL (polynomial de Rham forms), commutative cochain algebras in rational homotopy theory; divided-power variants (Cenkl–Porter style) in positive or mixed characteristic
ideas.usually_credited_to: D. Sullivan (Infinitesimal computations in topology, 1977; preprints from about 1970); Bousfield–Gugenheim 1976; divided-power forms: Cenkl–Porter and others, 1980s
ideas.where_published: Not known in published texts. Pursuing Stacks (1983) mentions related multiplicative and cochain questions, but I am unsure of any explicit mention of Sullivan.

missed.claim: Around 1975–76, Grothendieck explicitly links his theory of ∂-perfect semi-simplicial complexes with multiplicative structures to Sullivan's De Rham complex. He identifies divided powers as what replaces the characteristic-0 hypothesis. This is an early, independent framing of the 'divided-power de Rham forms for integral or mod p cochain models' line, though the idea later appeared in other hands.
missed.quote: Il y a donc un complexe de De Rham - Sullivan si la car. 0
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mainly of historical interest: it documents Grothendieck's awareness of rational homotopy theory and how he planned to extend it beyond characteristic 0. Modern work on integral or p-adic cochain models (Mandell, E∞, divided-power algebras) covers the mathematics.

deep.surprise_reason: A single, partly illegible two-line remark. The mathematics is standard (Sullivan forms exist in characteristic 0). The only interest is historical: Grothendieck connects his divided-power De Rham construction with Sullivan's theory.
transcription_corrections: Line 1 likely reads 'Il y a donc un complexe de' rather than 'Il y a de [?] — un complexe [?] de'.
Line 2 likely reads 'De Rham - Sullivan si la car. [=] 0.' The interlinear insertion '{+de la de+}' is probably 'si la car.', replacing a crossed-out word; the final 'con.' is probably 'car. 0'.
The rest of the page is show-through from the reverse side and should not be transcribed as content of this page.
